content: Looking forward does not mean staring at a single point the whole time. It means looking where you are going, where you are rotating, or where you are going to land, depending on the moment. When landing, 'forward' is the horizon, never the ground.

If you land on your feet, look forward or at the horizon, with your chest up and your stomach tight. If you use your hands or head to support yourself, yes, look at the support point, but protect yourself, and as soon as you stand up return to the front. If you look at your feet or the ground when you land, your chest drops.
Landing on your feet: gaze forward or at the horizon, chest up. Supporting with hands or head: look at the support point carefully and lift your gaze forward as you stand up.
